identification.summary: Smishing Triad is a name for a Chinese-speaking, financially motivated smishing and phishing-as-a-service ecosystem that impersonates postal, delivery, toll and banking brands to steal personal and payment data [S1][S3][S6]. Resecurity reported in 2023 that it sold smishing kits via Telegram and sent lures as iMessages from compromised Apple iCloud accounts [S1]. Silent Push (April 2025) reported targeting of at least 121 countries and a shift toward banking-phishing kits [S3]. Silent Push reported that in March 2025 the kit developer launched a Telegram channel for a new Lighthouse kit aimed at financial institutions [S3]; press coverage links Lighthouse to Smishing Triad [S4].
identification.firstObserved: Sources disagree: Silent Push says operating since 2023 [S3]; Brandefense says active since 2022 [S6]. Resecurity's USPS/iMessage reporting dates to 2023 [S1].
identification.notes: Cluster boundary: some coverage treats Lighthouse as the same group renamed, others as one of several Smishing Triad operations [S4]. Darcula/Magic Cat and Lucid are described as separate, interconnected China-based kits, not merged here [S4][S5]. This is a criminal PhaaS ecosystem, not a state actor; no Microsoft Typhoon/Storm name or MITRE group was found.

attribution.sponsor: No state sponsor identified in the sources gathered. Described as a financially motivated cybercrime group [S6].
attribution.confidence: Brandefense describes a base in China and Southeast Asia with affiliates in the UAE, Egypt and India [S6]. Cisco Talos, as relayed by press, links the Lighthouse kit to a developer using the alias Wang Duo Yu (also CoSmile) [S4]. Google's suit names 25 unidentified John Doe defendants, so no individuals are formally identified [S4][S5].
attribution.basis: Vendor research (Resecurity, Silent Push, Brandefense) and Google's civil complaint as reported by press [S1][S3][S4][S5][S6].

objectives: Financial gain: harvesting personally identifying information, payment-card data and banking credentials, and selling kits and services to other criminals [S1][S3][S6].

sectors: Postal and delivery services (as impersonated brands)
regions: Global; at least 121 countries per Silent Push [S3]
United States, United Kingdom, Poland, Sweden, Italy, Indonesia, Malaysia, Japan [S1]
targeting.notes: Victims are consumers; brands are impersonated rather than breached [S1][S3]. Resecurity also reported code injection into online shops to capture customer data [S1]. UAE lures were geofenced to UAE IPs [S2].

capabilities.summary: Resecurity (2023) reported iMessage delivery from compromised iCloud accounts, kits sold on Telegram from $200 per month, a Telegram channel of over 2,725 members, domains mostly in the .top zone registered via NameSilo and fronted by Cloudflare, and an SQL injection flaw in one kit that exposed data on over 108,000 victims [S1]. In the UAE, Resecurity reported lookalike domains registered via Gname.com, geofencing, use of purchased UAE resident databases and previously compromised iCloud accounts [S2]. Silent Push reported up to 100,000 texts per day and banking-phishing kits first seen March 2025 [S3]. Google says the successor Lighthouse kit offered at least 107 templates and was sold by subscription [S4][S5].

campaigns.name: Google civil suit against Lighthouse operators
campaigns.summary: Google filed in the Southern District of New York on 12 November 2025 against 25 John Does under RICO, the Lanham Act and the CFAA, citing over a million victims in 120 countries.

diamond.adversary: Chinese-speaking criminal operators and developers (alias Wang Duo Yu/CoSmile reported by Talos via press) selling kits to affiliates [S4][S6].
diamond.capability: Smishing and iMessage lures, phishing-as-a-service kits sold on Telegram, banking-phishing kits [S1][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Rotating lookalike domains (.top via NameSilo, Cloudflare; Gname.com in UAE), compromised iCloud accounts, Telegram channels [S1][S2].
diamond.victim: Consumers across 100+ countries; impersonated postal, toll and banking brands [S1][S3][S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Profit-driven criminal ecosystem; no state tasking found in sources [S6].
diamond.technology: Consumer messaging channels (SMS, iMessage), mobile payment wallets, and weak sender verification [S1][S3].

gaps: Exact publication dates of the Resecurity USPS and UAE reports were not visible; dated 2023 only, from search snippets.
Primary documents (Google complaint, Krebs April 2025 article, Talos, Unit 42, Netcraft, Prodaft) were not opened; WebFetch failed. Claims about them come via press or search summaries.
Unit 42 and Thai CERT figures (about 194,000 domains) and Netcraft figures could not be tied to a fetched page and are omitted.
Relationship of Lighthouse, Lucid and Darcula to the Smishing Triad name is disputed among sources.
Link of the 2024 US toll campaign to this group rests on Google/Talos reporting via press.
Outcome of the Google lawsuit and any arrests are unknown.
No state tie, MITRE group ID or Microsoft name identified.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the personnel population's mobile messaging (SMS/iMessage), payment cards and bank accounts, not DoD networks. STEP 2: The adversary is a commodity PhaaS ecosystem with large volume and rapid domain rotation [S1][S3]. STEP 3: Template is lure text, lookalike page, card or credential capture, wallet provisioning [S3][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued brand-themed smishing (postal, toll, bank) against US and allied populations including service members. MDCOA is use of harvested identity data to target personnel or families for follow-on fraud or social engineering. Candidate indicators: new lookalike domains for relocation, tolls or military banks, iMessage lures from unknown Apple IDs, geofenced pages [S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track brand-impersonation reporting relevant to personnel finances. (2) Authorities: this is a criminal threat; response sits with law enforcement and commercial takedowns, with the force role limited to user guidance and reporting [S4]. (3) Mission assurance: low direct risk to operational networks, but compromised personal accounts and cards can affect personnel reliability. (4) Coordination: route reports to IC3 and service security awareness channels [S7].

provenance.importedSummary: The Smishing Triad is a Chinese-speaking threat group known for targeting postal services and their customers globally through smishing campaigns. They leverage compromised Apple iMessage accounts to send fraudulent messages warning of undeliverable packages, aiming to collect personally identifying information and payment credentials. The group offers smishing kits for sale on platforms like Telegram, enabling other cybercriminals to launch independent attacks. "Smishing Triad" has expanded its operations to target UAE citizens, using geo-filtering to focus on victims in the Emirates.
